questions.q: What did the psalmist ask Yahweh to remember?
questions.a: He asked Yahweh to remember David’s suffering and how David made a solemn promise to the Yahweh, the Mighty One who Jacob worshiped.

questions.q: David vowed that he would not enter his house or sleep until he did what?
questions.a: He said he would not rest until he built a home for Yahweh.

questions.q: Where will the people go and what will they do when they get there?
questions.a: They will go to the place where Yahweh lives and worship.

questions.q: What does the psalmist want the priests and the people to do?
questions.a: The psalmist wants the priests to always do what is right and the people who are faithful to Yahweh to shout joyfully.

questions.q: What does the psalmist ask Yahweh not to do, for the sake of David?
questions.a: The psalmist asks Yahweh not to reject David, the king whom he has chosen.

questions.q: What is the oath Yahweh swore to David?
questions.a: Yahweh promised that one of David’s own descendants would sit on his throne as king.

questions.q: What does Yahweh declare about Zion?
questions.a: Yahweh chose Zion as his dwelling place and declares that he will stay there forever.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do for the people of Zion?
questions.a: Yahweh will provide everything that the people of Zion need, so that even the poor who live there will have enough food to satisfy them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh promise the king?
questions.a: Yahweh will cause the enemies of the chosen king to be defeated and ashamed, but his kingdom will flourish.

commentary.text: Verses 1–10 David bound himself to find a place for the Lord, for the ark, the token of God's presence. When work is to be done for the Lord, it is good to tie ourselves to a time. It is good in the morning to fix upon work for the day, with submission to Providence, for we know not what a day may bring forth. And we should first, and without delay, seek to have our own hearts made a habitation of God through the Spirit. He prays that God would take up his dwelling in the habitation he had built; that he would give grace to the ministers of the sanctuary to do their duty. David pleads that he was the anointed of the Lord, and this he pleads as a type of Christ, the great Anointed. We have no merit of our own to plead; but, for His sake, in whom there is a fulness of merit, let us find favour. And every true believer in Christ, is an anointed one, and has received from the Holy One the oil of true grace. The request is, that God would not turn away, but hear and answer their petitions for his Son's sake.

The Lord never turns from us when we plead the covenant with his anointed Prophet, Priest, and King. How vast is the love of God to man, that he should speak thus concerning his church! It is his desire to dwell with us; yet how little do we desire to dwell with him! He abode in Zion till the sins of Israel caused him to give them up to the spoilers. Forsake us not, O God, and deliver us not in like manner, sinful though we are. God's people have a special blessing on common enjoyments, and that blessing puts peculiar sweetness into them. Zion's poor have reason to be content with a little of this world, because they have better things prepared for them. God will abundantly bless the nourishment of the new man, and satisfy the poor in spirit with the bread of life. He gives more than we ask, and when he gives salvation, he will give abundant joy. God would bring to nothing every design formed to destroy the house of David, until King Messiah should arise out of it, to sit upon the throne of his Father. In him all the promises centre. His enemies, who will not have him to reign over them, shall at the last day be clothed with shame and confusion for ever.
